evidence_against: The analyst’s characterization of repeated ETH DOWN and BTC RANGE candidates as stronger evidence may overstate replication. Candidate definitions, horizons, target units, settlement rules, and outcome overlap are absent; matching titles can indicate semantic duplication rather than independent confirmation.

The five highlighted candidate counts sum to 203 matured outcomes (48+46+41+37+31), exceeding architecture health’s total of 194 matured and adjudicated outcomes. This precludes interpreting those counts as independent observations without reconciling scope and overlap.

Selection occurred across 178 lifecycle candidates and 311 forecast JSON files, but no multiple-testing correction, family-wise error control, false-discovery estimate, or prespecified candidate-selection rule is supplied. Five supportive high-N labels could therefore reflect selection from a broad search.

MATURED_SUPPORTED is only a lifecycle label. There are no effect sizes, candidate losses, confidence intervals, calibration measures, hit rates, or baseline losses from which to determine whether support is economically or statistically meaningful.

The proposed “naïve unconditional baseline” is not operationally defined. Its estimation window, information set, update policy, regime treatment, and loss function remain unspecified, allowing baseline weakness or revision drift to manufacture apparent incremental value.

No candidate-level creation timestamps, immutable specifications, source-temporal-provenance records, or no-hindsight receipts are supplied. The frozen council package does not by itself establish that candidate definitions and evaluation rules were fixed before every scored observation.

The 62 archive-only duplicates and unspecified common market episodes create dependence risk. Concurrent observations from two candidates on the same instrument may represent repeated scoring of the same event rather than additional evidence.

Registry and escalation artifacts disagree on maturation counts for EC-0dc8abd903144198e36e (48 versus 46) and EC-0e9733866b37fcec87ed (11 versus 7), while scientific-admission status is null in one artifact and QUALIFIED_FOR_FORWARD_TEST in another. These lineage differences weaken count-based prioritization.

The BTC DOWN contrast is not yet symmetric: EC-62dc79b74bb6526e7c67 has 31 outcomes while EC-8136ca63303d3ccd5605 has 10. The observed ordering could be sampling instability, differing eligibility, or regime coincidence rather than stable definitional value.

All 125 assessed workflows are AMBER, and relevant adjudication, provenance, and council workflows report NO_RUN_HISTORY and/or WORKFLOW_NOT_REGISTERED_OR_API_UNAVAILABLE. The evidence cannot distinguish API-visibility problems from actual execution gaps.
evidence_for: The analyst appropriately declined to ratify a predictive rule, forecast, portfolio action, threshold change, weight change, or canonical promotion.

Five named forecast tests are labeled MATURED_SUPPORTED with registry counts above the supplied 25-outcome policy minimum, making them eligible for adversarial examination even though the labels do not establish incremental value.

Experiment receipt synchronization reports PASS with zero hash mismatches, and the shadow-registry summary reports zero source-missing candidates; these are limited integrity signals rather than performance evidence.
The supplied package explicitly preserves candidates as non-canonical and non-executing and states that baseline, control, regime, and complexity review remains outstanding.
The monthly, maturation, milestone, and escalation triggers are active, supporting a research-only review despite unresolved evidence quality.
hypotheses: Conditional on recovering immutable pre-outcome specifications, each of EC-4e02e53e58c3e79ba871 and EC-5c8b675adec8111650dd will separately achieve lower mean prospective loss than the same precisely defined unconditional baseline over at least 25 new candidate-eligible, temporally forward, non-duplicate settlements per candidate. The loss function, baseline estimation window, overlap policy, and settlement rules must be frozen before observation. Falsified if either candidate fails to improve on the baseline or if improvement disappears after common-episode dependence controls.

Conditional on recovering immutable pre-outcome specifications, each of EC-0dc8abd903144198e36e and EC-23f2161a31fe1f482e99 will separately achieve lower mean prospective loss than the same precisely defined unconditional RANGE baseline over at least 25 new candidate-eligible, temporally forward, non-duplicate settlements per candidate. Falsified if either candidate has non-positive incremental improvement or if apparent improvement depends on duplicate or overlapping settlements.

On a prospectively frozen common eligible cohort of at least 25 paired settlements, BTC DOWN candidate EC-62dc79b74bb6526e7c67 will have lower mean loss than EC-8136ca63303d3ccd5605 under one preregistered scoring rule. Falsified if no common cohort can be defined without revising either candidate, if the loss difference is non-positive, or if the ordering is attributable to duplicated settlements.
adversarial.summary: The analyst’s refusal to ratify a market rule survives adversarial review, but the claim that repeated ETH DOWN and BTC RANGE candidates constitute stronger evidence does not yet survive. Their apparent replication may be semantic and outcome-dependent: the five highlighted counts total 203, already exceeding the architecture-wide total of 194 matured and adjudicated outcomes. Broad candidate selection, missing effect sizes and baselines, unresolved lineage discrepancies, absent no-hindsight documentation, and workflow visibility warnings prevent a predictive learning claim. The named candidates remain bounded research objects suitable only for fresh candidate-level tests with frozen specifications, exact baselines, duplicate controls, and non-overlapping prospective observations.
uncertainties: It is unknown whether identically titled candidates differ in horizon, target magnitude, data source, eligibility rule, settlement rule, or scoring method.
The relationship among 286 outcome JSON files, a matured-outcome delta of 286, and 194 matured/adjudicated outcomes is unresolved.
Outcome-level overlap cannot be measured from the supplied candidate aggregates, and the five high-N counts exceeding 194 may reflect overlap, scope differences, or inconsistent snapshots.
No supplied record establishes when each candidate specification was frozen relative to its scored observations, so hindsight leakage cannot be excluded.
The statistical meaning of MATURED_SUPPORTED and MATURED_NOT_SUPPORTED is unspecified, including whether labels incorporate multiplicity or dependence.
Regime coverage, market-episode concentration, and effective sample sizes are unknown.
Automation warnings may represent unavailable API registration rather than non-execution; operational reliability therefore remains indeterminate.
No supplied evidence connects forecast-test performance to execution feasibility, costs, portfolio utility, or causal mechanism.

Their definitions may differ, so neither pooling nor contradiction resolution is justified.
Most candidates remain immature or unresolved: 93 are INCUBATING, 24 WAITING_FOR_MAPPING, 7 WAITING_FOR_DATA, 32 MATURED_INCONCLUSIVE, and 8 TARGET_UNIT_QUARANTINED.
Many apparent results are small-N. Supported candidates with 1, 2, or 11 matured outcomes do not meet the supplied minimum of 25 outcomes for a learning claim.

Evidence counts disagree across artifacts: 286 outcome JSON files and a matured-outcome delta of 286 contrast with 194 matured/adjudicated outcomes in architecture health. Candidate counts also differ for EC-0dc8abd903144198e36e (48 versus 46) and EC-0e9733866b37fcec87ed (11 versus 7).
The weekly adjudication identifies 62 archive-only duplicates. Independence and overlap among candidate outcomes are not reported, limiting interpretation of nominal sample sizes.
Scientific-admission status is null in the experiment registry but QUALIFIED_FOR_FORWARD_TEST in the escalation queue, indicating snapshot or lineage disagreement.
Automation health is AMBER for all 125 assessed workflows, with widespread NO_RUN_HISTORY and WORKFLOW_NOT_REGISTERED_OR_API_UNAVAILABLE findings, including the monthly council workflow.

evidence_for: The monthly, maturation, milestone, and escalation triggers are all active for 2026-09, so a research-only audit is due.
The architecture-health artifact reports 194 matured and adjudicated outcomes, zero censored outcomes, and a 0.0 censor rate within its stated 14-day evidence window.

Five specific frozen forecast tests exceed the supplied 25-outcome minimum and are labeled MATURED_SUPPORTED: BTC RANGE EC-0dc8abd903144198e36e, ETH DOWN EC-4e02e53e58c3e79ba871, ETH DOWN EC-5c8b675adec8111650dd, BTC RANGE EC-23f2161a31fe1f482e99, and BTC DOWN EC-62dc79b74bb6526e7c67.

The two repeated higher-N families—ETH mark-price DOWN and BTC mark-price RANGE—each contain two supported candidates with more than 25 matured outcomes, making them stronger research subjects than isolated small-N patterns.

hypotheses: New preregistered hypothesis: the frozen ETH mark-price DOWN candidate family represented by EC-4e02e53e58c3e79ba871 and EC-5c8b675adec8111650dd will produce lower mean prospective loss than a naïve unconditional baseline over at least 25 new, independent, concurrently settled observations, using candidate settlement rules and a loss function frozen before observation. Falsified if the family’s mean loss is not lower than the baseline or if the result depends on only one candidate.

New preregistered hypothesis: the frozen BTC mark-price RANGE candidate family represented by EC-0dc8abd903144198e36e and EC-23f2161a31fe1f482e99 will produce lower mean prospective loss than a naïve unconditional baseline over at least 25 new, independent, concurrently settled observations, with overlap handling, settlement rules, and loss function frozen in advance. Falsified if incremental loss improvement is non-positive or disappears after duplicate and overlap controls.

New preregistered adversarial hypothesis: the disagreement between supported BTC DOWN candidate EC-62dc79b74bb6526e7c67 and not-supported BTC DOWN candidate EC-8136ca63303d3ccd5605 reflects stable differences in their frozen definitions rather than sampling instability. Evaluate both concurrently on at least 25 new eligible observations without modifying either test. Falsified if the supported candidate fails to retain a lower preregistered prospective loss than the not-supported candidate or if their ordering reverses across predefined regime strata.
analyst.summary: The audit can distinguish evidence maturity but cannot ratify a predictive learning claim. Five specific derivatives tests exceed the 25-outcome policy minimum and carry supportive prospective labels, with repeated higher-N evidence in ETH DOWN and BTC RANGE families. What was challenged is generalization: related candidates also failed, many results are small-N or quarantined, and no baseline, effect-size, regime, complexity, or independence diagnostics are supplied. What remains unlearned is whether any candidate adds out-of-sample information beyond a naïve baseline, whether support is regime-stable, and whether duplicate outcomes inflate counts. The 62 archive-only duplicates are explicitly redundant. The highest-information bounded question is whether the repeated ETH DOWN and BTC RANGE families retain incremental prospective value under frozen baseline, overlap, and adversarial controls. No forecast, portfolio action, rule change, weight change, threshold change, or canonical promotion is supported.
uncertainties: The supplied artifacts do not reconcile the 286 outcome files and matured delta with the 194 matured/adjudicated outcomes reported by architecture health.
Candidate-level maturation counts differ between the registry and escalation queue for at least two named candidates.
Outcome independence, duplicate overlap, cohort timing, and exposure to common market episodes are unspecified.
Original candidate horizons, target values or ranges, settlement rules, and scoring metrics are absent from the supplied evidence.
The meaning and comparability of MATURED_SUPPORTED across candidates cannot be verified without candidate-specific performance records.
Automation registration and run-history warnings may reflect API visibility limitations rather than actual workflow non-execution; the supplied data does not resolve this.
No evidence establishes causal mechanisms, portfolio utility, execution feasibility, or stability outside the observed prospective cohorts.
